title: Given a string, find the length of its longest palindromic subsequence, where a subsequence keeps relative order but need not be contiguous. Explain the Palindromic Subsequence DP pattern, the recurrence, the complexity, and a banking use case.
shortTitle: Longest Palindromic Subsequence (Longest Subsequence That Reads the Same Both Ways)

s1_definition.profdef: The Longest Palindromic Subsequence is the canonical Palindromic Subsequence pattern problem. We compare the two ends of a range: if the characters match, they both belong to the palindrome and we add two to the best of the inner range, otherwise we drop one end or the other and take the larger. This two-ended recurrence gives a quadratic time and space dynamic program.
s1_definition.analogy: The National Bank of India stores a reference code on each transaction and wants the longest symmetric core inside it, because symmetric cores are used as a lightweight integrity marker. Rajesh and Priya each have a code, and the bank measures how long a code reads the same forward and backward when you are allowed to skip characters.
s1_definition.oneliner: If the ends match add two to the inner answer, otherwise drop one end and keep the better of the two.
s1_definition.raw:
**Professional definition:** The Longest Palindromic Subsequence is the canonical Palindromic Subsequence pattern problem. We compare the two ends of a range: if the characters match, they both belong to the palindrome and we add two to the best of the inner range, otherwise we drop one end or the other and take the larger. This two-ended recurrence gives a quadratic time and space dynamic program.

**In simple words (banking analogy):** The National Bank of India stores a reference code on each transaction and wants the longest symmetric core inside it, because symmetric cores are used as a lightweight integrity marker. Rajesh and Priya each have a code, and the bank measures how long a code reads the same forward and backward when you are allowed to skip characters.

**One line to remember:** If the ends match add two to the inner answer, otherwise drop one end and keep the better of the two.

sections.s2_technical:
We define the answer for a range as the longest palindromic subsequence inside the substring from index i to index j. When the character at i equals the character at j, those two characters wrap a palindrome, so the answer is two plus the answer for the inner range i plus one to j minus one. When they differ, at least one of them cannot be an outer pair, so the answer is the larger of the range i plus one to j and the range i to j minus one. A single character is a palindrome of length one, which seeds the diagonal.

Bottom-up we fill a two dimensional table by increasing range length: `for (int i = n - 1; i >= 0; i--) { dp[i][i] = 1; for (int j = i + 1; j < n; j++) dp[i][j] = s.charAt(i) == s.charAt(j) ? 2 + dp[i+1][j-1] : Math.max(dp[i+1][j], dp[i][j-1]); }` and the answer is `dp[0][n-1]`. A concrete check: for the code where the symmetric core spans several characters, the table converges from short ranges outward. Senior nuance: this is quadratic in time and space, the subsequence version differs from the substring version because gaps are allowed, and you can recover the actual subsequence by walking the table from the corner.
sections.s3_banking:
Problem 1 — The National Bank of India tags each transaction with a reference code and uses the longest symmetric core inside the code as a lightweight integrity marker, so it needs to measure, for a given code, the longest sequence of characters that reads the same forward and backward when skipping is allowed. Checking every subsequence is exponential. This is exactly how the Longest Palindromic Subsequence works: it finds that length with the two-ended recurrence in quadratic time.

The code defines a `ReferenceCodeService` exposing `longestPalindromicCore(code)` returning the length of the longest palindromic subsequence. A `Demo` runs it over a sample reference code and logs the length.

sections.s5_journey:
The input is the reference code RABCBAR. We want the longest subsequence that reads the same both ways.

Step 1 — We fill short ranges first. Every single character gets length one along the diagonal of the table.

Step 2 — For adjacent pairs, matching characters give two and differing pairs give one. The pair BC gives one, while equal neighbours would give two.

Step 3 — For the inner stretch ABCBA the ends A and A match, so the answer is two plus the core of BCB. The core of BCB has matching ends B and B giving two plus the single C, which is three, so ABCBA yields five.

Step 4 — For the full code RABCBAR the ends R and R match, so the answer is two plus the core of ABCBA which is five, giving seven.

Step 5 — The corner cell holds seven, so the entire code is itself a palindrome of length seven. The output is below.

```
Oct 27, 2026 9:05:11 PM com.bank.refcode.service.ReferenceCodeService longestPalindromicCore
INFO: Longest palindromic core of RABCBAR = 7
Oct 27, 2026 9:05:11 PM com.bank.refcode.ReferenceCodeApplication main
INFO: Integrity core length for code RABCBAR is 7
```
sections.s5b_flow:
```
  Input: code = "RABCBAR"
    │
    ▼
  fill diagonal: every single char = 1
    │ ends match → 2 + inner(i+1, j-1)
    │ ends differ → max(inner(i+1,j), inner(i,j-1))
    │ ABCBA → A==A → 2 + core(BCB)=3 → 5
    │ RABCBAR → R==R → 2 + core(ABCBA)=5 → 7
    ▼
  Output: longest palindromic core = 7
```

sections.s6_takeaway:
The Longest Palindromic Subsequence is the canonical Palindromic Subsequence pattern problem, and the key insight is that I reason about a range by its two ends. If the character at the left end equals the character at the right end, those two characters form the outer layer of a palindrome, so the answer is two plus the longest palindromic subsequence of the inner range. If the ends differ, at least one of them cannot be part of an outer pair, so I drop one end and take the larger of the two shorter ranges.

I build this bottom-up in a two dimensional table, seeding the diagonal with one because any single character is a palindrome, and then filling ranges of increasing length so that every inner range is ready before the range that depends on it. The answer sits in the corner cell spanning the whole string. This runs in quadratic time and space, and I always clarify that the subsequence version allows gaps, which is what distinguishes it from the contiguous substring version.

At the National Bank of India I used this to measure the longest symmetric core inside each transaction reference code, because the bank used that symmetric core as a lightweight integrity marker. I ran the two-ended range dynamic program over each code and returned the length. Explaining the match-the-ends recurrence, the increasing-length fill order, and the distinction from the substring version is what shows an interviewer that I genuinely understand the Palindromic Subsequence pattern behind the Longest Palindromic Subsequence.
